channel.title: The Local Europe - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local Europe (thelocal.com)

item.title: 'I miss friendly people': The reasons foreigners in Austria choose to leave
item.description: Austria has a lot to offer foreign residents but not everyone wants to stay forever. Whether its family, taxes or politics, many foreigners reach a point when they decide it's better to leave.

item.title: Births rise in Spain for first time in over a decade
item.description: The number of babies born in Spain rose slightly for the first time in more than a decade in 2025, official data showed Wednesday, a boost for a country facing one of Europe's most serious demographic crises.

item.title: OPINION: Macron's offer to 'extend' the French nuclear umbrella to Europe is fraught with problems
item.description: Sharing umbrellas is never easy. France has offered to 'extend' its nuclear umbrella to other European countries without actually 'sharing' it. How can that work, asks John Lichfield.

item.title: How UK dual nationals in Europe can renounce British citizenship
item.description: If you wish to give up British citizenship - here's how to do it, how much it costs and how, in some cases, you can get it back.

item.title: PODCAST: France fears more political violence and record rainfall leaves the country under water
item.description: The Talking France podcast is back looking at the storms - both meteorological and political - that have gripped France this week, plus the country's biggest farm show and those pesky French 'false friends'.

item.title: In pictures: NATO troops storm Germany's Baltic coast in training exercise
item.description: Thousands of NATO troops including from Spain and Turkey joined an exercise Wednesday on Germany's Baltic coast that defence officials labelled a show of readiness to deter Russia.

item.title: French transport police to trial stun guns on trains
item.description: Several hundred officers who police France's trains and the Paris Metro are to be armed with stun guns on an experimental basis in a bid to increase security, Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said on Thursday.

item.title: Eurostar station boss pledges to cut boarding times
item.description: Passengers on the Eurostar could be spared the airport-style waiting times in the future, as bosses at London St Pancras station pledge to cut boarding times for cross-Channel passengers.

item.title: 'Systemic failures' led to Louvre robbery, inquiry finds
item.description: "Systemic failures" led to the €88-million robbery at the Louvre museum in Paris last year, MPs leading an inquiry said on Thursday, raising pressure on embattled director Laurence des Cars.

item.title: 36 days and counting: When will it ever stop raining in France?
item.description: With France having already broken a record for 36 consecutive days of rain the question being asked, in increasingly shrill tones, is when will the wet weather end?
